result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.
Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.

result.rule: When the description lists several activities that all belong to one stage, have no stated order between them, and a later step waits until every one of them has finished: Model each listed activity as its own task. Open the branches with a parallel gateway placed before the first of these tasks, and close them with a matching parallel gateway placed before the next step. Do not sequence the tasks unless the description states an order, and do not merge them into one task.

When the description lists several activities that all follow the same preceding event and are performed together, and a later step continues only after all of them are done: Model an opening parallel gateway after the preceding step, with one branch per listed activity, and close those branches with a joining parallel gateway before the next step. Do not chain the activities in sequence, and do not use an exclusive gateway to join them.

When the description lists several activities in one sentence, performed by the same actor or team, and states no concurrency, order condition, or synchronization between them: Model the listed activities as consecutive tasks in the order the text gives, connected by sequence flows. Do not insert a parallel gateway unless the description states that the activities run at the same time or must all finish before the next step.

When the description states one step in which a participant performs two distinct actions joined by 'and', and the second action has its own purpose or result that is not part of the first: Model each distinct action as its own bpmn:task, in the order the description gives, on the sequence flow where the step occurs. Give each task a label that names only its own action. Do not combine the actions into one task label, and do not drop the second action because the first action's label seems to cover it.

result.rule: Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Do not infer a task subtype only from a verb in its label; require supporting meaning in the full description.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use data input and output associations between data and activities. Data associations do not define execution order.
